summary: Compact hosted API demo focused on chat generation basics: how streaming works in practice, which generation parameters matter for Kepler's use case, and recommended retry/fallback patterns. SE ran a live SDK demo showing streaming fragments, client-side assembly, and a graceful fallback to non-streaming with a config toggle.
meeting_header:
Date: 2025-11-05 | Start: 16:23 PST | Duration: 42m
Redwood: Alex Murphy (AE), Samira Patel (SE), Ravi Desai (Support)
Kepler Health: Jordan Lee (Eng Lead), Priya Natarajan (ML Eng), Ethan Morales (Product), Marta Silva (Security)
transcript:
00:00 Alex (Redwood AE): hey folks, thanks for joining, i'm Alex, i'll kick things off. today we're gonna walk through hosted chat generation: basic params, how streaming actually looks, and what to do when things fail.
00:18 Jordan (Kepler): hi thanks, we have 40 minutes, mainly interested in low-latency answers for diagnostics and a fallback for offline mode. also concerned about audit logs.
00:34 Samira (Redwood SE): cool, i'll run the demo. quick note, i'll be using the JS SDK and curl snippets. apologies if i garble any code, the transcript will be a bit rough.
00:50 Alex: quick qualification — what's your expected qps and SLO?
01:05 Jordan: baseline is 20 requests/sec during peak, p99 latency target around 300-400ms. accuracy is more important than hallucinations, so we want conservative sampling.
01:22 Priya: and for data residency, some PHI might stay in the prompt. Marta will need to confirm compliance.
01:31 Marta: yes, SOC2 plus KMS integration are blockers. we need audit logs for token-level retention.
01:45 Alex: got it. we'll cover the console observability and KMS briefly at the end. Samira, demo?
01:52 Samira: yep. i'm going to show a small node script that calls the hosted /v1/chat endpoint with streaming. code: (paraphrased) const r = await client.chat.stream({model: 'redwood-large', messages, temperature: 0.2, max_tokens: 150});
02:20 Samira: first thing folks notice is streaming returns chunks. on the client you get partial deltas and you assemble them. this reduces perceived latency because you see tokens earlier.
02:37 Ethan (Product): is streaming SSE or websockets?
02:44 Samira: we support server-sent events in the HTTP path and streaming over the SDK so it looks like an async iterator in JS. websockets are coming in some private setups but for hosted it's SSE-ish. (note: sometimes transcriber shows "S S E" or "SSE-ee").
03:05 Samira: i'll intentionally add a retry scenario: i'll drop a chunk. watch how the SDK retries at the request layer with exponential backoff and a jitter.
03:23 (demo noise, brief screen share change)
03:38 Samira: here, you see the client emits partial: ".patient has a history of" then later "hypertension and diabetes" — if a chunk fails mid-stream the SDK will attempt a short retry but we also recommend idempotency keys to avoid double side effects.
03:59 Priya: how do you suggest composing idempotency for chat? session id + last timestamp?
04:10 Samira: common pattern: conversation_id + request_hash. for safety you can mark stateful calls as non-idempotent and only retry in read-only generations. we also expose a resume token for long responses in Dedicated/private.
04:34 Jordan: what's the max_tokens default?
04:40 Samira: default 256, but you can set max_tokens param. note: cost is linear with tokens generated and consumed in context.
04:51 Samira: i'll change temperature to 0.0 then 0.8 to show difference. low temp = deterministic, higher temp = more diverse.
05:10 (audio lag)
05:17 Samira: here's a sample: temp 0.0 -> more conservative phrasing, temp 0.8 -> more speculative language. for Kepler, given need to avoid hallucinations, we recommend temp 0.0-0.2 and top_p 0.7-0.9 depending on prompt.
05:41 Jordan: ok we want conservative.
05:46 Alex: there's also nucleus sampling via top_p. you can combine with temperature.
05:54 Samira: on retries: the SDK uses client-side retry with exponential backoff and respects idempotency headers. server-side we provide graceful degradation: if a model variant is down we can fallback to a smaller quantized variant to keep latency bounded but quality drops.
06:18 Priya: can we route to dedicated if we hit a spike?
06:23 Alex: yes, with routing policy you can prefer dedicated pool for mission-critical requests; hosted will fallback to dedicated or vice versa per policy.
06:33 Samira: now i'll show a failure case. i'll force a timeout and show how the client app replays a request safely if it's idempotent.
07:00 Samira: (typing) curl -X POST ... -H 'Idempotency-Key: abc123' ... 
07:12 Jordan: is retry count configurable?
07:15 Samira: yes, client has max_retries and per-retry delay; server-side also has policy for transient errors vs 4xx which are not retried.
07:28 Ethan: what about token streaming order? do you always get tokens in order?
07:33 Samira: yes, streaming preserves token order. note: partial transcripts sometimes mis-order if you concatenate chunks incorrectly on the client. library handles that for you but if you implement raw SSE be cautious.
07:56 (crosstalk)
08:10 Samira: switching to console: show logs — per-request token breakdown, cost estimate, p50/p95/p99 latency. you can filter by api_key or route.
08:31 Alex: we'll attach a console screenshot in follow-up.
08:37 Priya: can we set per-route quotas?
08:39 Alex: yes, rate-limits and quotas per API key or per customer route.
08:45 Marta: about encryption at rest: KMS integration?
08:49 Alex: we integrate with customer-managed keys for Private; for hosted we offer managed KMS but can support bring-your-own for Private. we'll send the KMS matrix in the follow-up.
09:02 Samira: back to streaming: i want to highlight partial prefix caching. if many users ask the same initial prompt we can cache the computed KV prefix and reduce compute. that reduces cost and latency for repeat prompts. (note: sometimes transcribed as "KV cash")
09:33 Jordan: is that safe for PHI?
09:36 Marta: that's my worry.
09:38 Samira: we can configure cache policies per route and opt-out for PHI routes; and in Private you can fully disable caching.
09:50 Priya: what about concurrency limits per GPU?
09:53 Samira: runtime exposes concurrency per model variant; we give recommended settings based on batch sizes and latencies. we'll provide a tuning doc.
10:12 (10:12-minute mark, brief pause)
10:25 Samira: let me change the payload to show top_p effect. you'll see the tokens diverge.
10:42 (demo continues, short silence)
11:05 Jordan: can you show an example retry header coming back?
11:10 Samira: yes, response has x-retry-attempt and we surface it in SDK events. here's an example: x-retry-attempt: 1, x-request-id: r-abc.
11:33 Priya: what's recommended backoff strategy?
11:37 Samira: exponential with jitter; typical base 100-200ms, cap at 3s and 3 attempts for streaming. for non-streaming batch generation you might allow longer.
12:02 Ethan: curious about billing visibility — want to map tokens to customer features.
12:09 Alex: console has per-route token breakdown and per-api-key spend. you can export CSV for finance.
12:22 Samira: demo: forcing a model fallback to quantized smaller variant — you see latency drop but also model answers become terser.
12:45 Jordan: what are the recommended fallbacks for critical paths?
12:50 Samira: prefer smaller variant with same architecture if available; otherwise fallback to cached response or predefined fallback text. use canary rollouts before switching permanently.
13:10 (background noise, someone types)
13:30 Samira: small note about truncation: if context is larger than model window, we truncate older messages. we recommend summarizing older turns to stay in window.
13:49 Priya: do you provide auto-summarization helpers?
13:52 Samira: yes, Optimize has a helper but we'll demo a simple summarization call later.
14:05 Alex: let's address security questions quickly. Marta?
14:12 Marta: need to know log retention, SSO, RBAC roles.
14:18 Alex: we support SAML SSO, fine-grained RBAC, audit logs and configurable retention windows. i'll attach the security pack.
14:30 Samira: returning to retries — important to distinguish idempotent and non-idempotent: e.g., calls that trigger external side effects should be executed once. we provide guidance in our SDK and recommend request-level idempotency keys.
14:57 Jordan: how do you surface partial errors in streaming?
15:02 Samira: SDK emits an error event and a final status; you can choose to show partial content or discard depending on your UX. we also expose granular error codes for throttling vs transient infra failures.
15:32 (client question)
15:40 Priya: can we set per-model temperature limits to prevent too-high randomness?
15:44 Alex: yes, you can set policy-level overrides to clamp temperature or disallow certain models.
15:56 Samira: note about prompt injection: we have content filters and allow customers to plug their own filters in Private.
16:10 (16m mark)
16:18 Samira: now i'll show a scripted sequence: step 1 stream answer, step 2 if stream fails retry with idempotency, step 3 if still fails fall back to a short cached answer.
16:40 Jordan: will fallback to cached answer be acceptable in clinical setting? maybe only as a read-only hint, not a diagnosis.
16:51 Marta: exactly, fallback needs explicit UI disclaimers and audit trail.
17:05 Samira: we log fallback events in console with reason codes so you can review.
17:21 Alex: any other blockers from your side?
17:26 Priya: timeline: want POC in two weeks to validate latency and hallucination metrics.
17:34 Alex: we can provision test keys and a small hosted quota for that POC.
17:42 Samira: i'll prepare a sample workload runner to push 25 qps and log p99 — that'll be our spike test.
18:00 Ethan: what's the expected cost model for hosted during POC?
18:05 Alex: per-token pricing; we'll send a rough estimate based on expected qps and token size.
18:16 (small pause)
18:30 Samira: one more technical bit: continuous batching in runtime — we batch short-window requests to improve throughput but keep latency low. you can tune batching window and batch size per model.
18:52 Jordan: does batching increase tokenization overhead?
18:56 Samira: minor overhead, but per-token compute is amortized across requests so overall cost drops.
19:10 Priya: okay can we get default tuning values?
19:14 Samira: yes, we'll share a tuning guide with recommended batch sizes for each model family.
19:28 (screen share ends briefly)
19:40 Samira: demo wrap: i'll push the sample code and a short video to the shared drive.
19:47 Alex: recap: we'll send pricing + security pack, Samira will share streaming SDK snippet and spike test harness, Priya will send prompt set and SLOs.
20:02 Jordan: thanks, that helps.
20:10 Marta: once we get docs we'll schedule a deeper compliance call.
20:16 Alex: great. any final quick questions?
20:22 Priya: not from me.
20:25 Ethan: all good.
20:28 Alex: thanks everyone, we'll follow up via email and add action items to the CRM.
20:32 (meeting ends — small crosstalk, people say thanks)
